ActForm.description: What kind of act a governed call is.
ActForm.title: ActForm

AdmissionCheck.description: The checks admission runs, in order; each refuses before the next.
AdmissionCheck.title: AdmissionCheck

AgentContextProfiles.description: The optional conventions and project instructions context block.

instructions.description: The project's instructions: each `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` from the repository root that contains the workspace down to the workspace, in that order, each `path` relative to the repository root.

memory.description: The workspace's `MEMORY.md`, in envelopes recorded before hosts carried memory themselves. runx writes none: memory a host supplies travels as admitted context entries.

AgentContextProfiles.title: AgentContextProfiles

environment.description: Each variable the act declares, whether it's required, and whether it's available: the declaration itself, by name, never by value.

AllowedOperation.description: One connector operation a turn may call, named by the requirement that binds its instance.
AllowedOperation.title: AllowedOperation

currency.description: Provider currency/asset code; financial authority uses its canonical uppercase code, so a provider's lowercase `usd` still means USD cents.

units.description: Exact integer smallest units sent to the provider, or the exact bound maximum a protocol's settlement operation is allowed to spend.

ArtifactImplementation.description: The runtime's artifact space: one bounded value stored under the runx account the runtime is signed in as, keyed by the call's idempotency key and confirmed by reading its reference back.
ArtifactImplementation.title: ArtifactImplementation

Assessment.description: One answer to one criterion, with the references to the sealed calls or receipts the evaluator obtained against this subject. A `not_met` answer says what failed, and a `met` one has nothing to say.
Assessment.title: Assessment

AssessmentFailure.description: What failed: what was expected, what happened, and where. The criterion says what failed.
AssessmentFailure.title: AssessmentFailure

AttestationDecision.description: Whether the attestation can be sealed, or what it waits on.
AttestationDecision.title: AttestationDecision

AttestationEvidence.description: One opaque evidence locator, its digest, and what it is asserted to prove.
AttestationEvidence.title: AttestationEvidence

AttestationGap.description: Why an attestation is not ready to seal.
AttestationGap.title: AttestationGap

AttestationProofBoundary.description: What an attestation does not prove: runx called no provider, appended to no external ledger, and verified nothing outside itself. The parent receipt's seal is the only signature evidence.
AttestationProofBoundary.title: AttestationProofBoundary

packages.description: The packages every call's chain must be covered by, in any order (D31). An absent bound covers nothing, as every bound does, so a delegation states its own and an execution term names its chain. A package is listed once.

scopes.description: Grant scopes, in an operation's `scopes` vocabulary, such as `repo.read`.

term.description: The capability or delegation term, sealed so the subset proofs can be re-checked offline. Approvals carry no term.

AuthorityEvidenceKind.description: The three kinds of evidence admission proves. Each has one job.
AuthorityEvidenceKind.title: AuthorityEvidenceKind

AuthorityUseLimit.description: How many times a term may be used. An execution term is single use. Usage is reserved atomically with each effect attempt, never counted from receipts.
AuthorityUseLimit.title: AuthorityUseLimit

BoundAnswer.description: An agent's answer to an input request or an agent act.

request_digest.description: The digest of the request answered, as the run reported it.

BoundAnswer.title: BoundAnswer

BoundApproval.description: A person's decision, validated against the request it answers: an approval takes `approved` and `reason`, and a purchase's also the `choice` of method it pays with; a claimed call's retry takes `value: {"retry": true}`.

choice.description: The instance of the purchase request's method the person pays with.

BoundApproval.title: BoundApproval

BoundClosure.description: The exact package and execution closure a load bound for one method.
BoundClosure.title: BoundClosure

decision.description: The decision the call carries out.

form.description: What kind of act the call is.

previous.description: The receipt of the act this one follows.

reason.description: What a reader is told about this particular call.

target.description: The locator of what the act is about.

CallCost.description: What a sealed call cost, as its packet carries it. The quote is the operation's declared charge; the settled amount is what the call was charged, or `None` while that is unresolved.
CallCost.title: CallCost

methods.description: A skill's methods, each with its purpose when its source states one.

package.description: What a load and `registry.inspect` take: the registry package (`<publisher>/<name>@<version>`), or the project package's path in the workspace.

CatalogMethod.description: One method of a skill, as a model chooses it from an index.

purpose.description: What it does and when to use it, as its package states it.

CatalogMethod.title: CatalogMethod

CatalogPackageKind.description: What a skill or connector is, as the catalog lists it.
CatalogPackageKind.title: CatalogPackageKind

CatalogRule.description: What a load admits: exactly one of `catalog`, the registry's packages at a trust tier or above, and `project: true`, the packages the project authored that reach only the connectors the turn already reaches; one that reaches another waits on the person's trust. A registry package the project installed keeps its registry identity, so only `catalog` admits it.
CatalogRule.title: CatalogRule

CatalogSource.description: Where a package is: the registry publishes it, or the project authored it.
CatalogSource.title: CatalogSource

trust.description: The lowest tier a load admits on its own; a package below it waits on the person's trust.

CliHelpFlag.description: The form a CLI is asked for its help in.
CliHelpFlag.title: CliHelpFlag

CommandDecision.description: How an execution ended: it completed, it failed, or it was stopped.
CommandDecision.title: CommandDecision

CommandOutputMode.description: How a command's output is returned: its digest only, as text, or parsed as JSON.
CommandOutputMode.title: CommandOutputMode

ConnectorAuth.description: How a principal's authority over the provider is held. Every key is an alternative; placements say which ones they accept.

delegated.description: A hosted grant brokered by runx Connect. Valid only on the hosted placement; the OSS contract never describes the brokerage.

none.description: A public API with no credential.

session.description: Authority held by a local session the runtime can identify.

ConnectorAuth.title: ConnectorAuth

readiness.description: Each operation as ready as the project leaves it; none for a connector the project does not hold.

ConnectorOperation.description: One named action on a connector.

cost.description: What the provider charges per call; absent when no charge is known.

credentials.description: Named credentials that may authorize this operation (any of).

effect.description: What a successful write produced, as the reference its act's receipt carries.

guarantees.description: What the provider guarantees for this operation. Shared mechanics never assume more, and a use never tolerates more.

implementation.description: How the local placement runs it. The hosted placement runs an `http` implementation through the provider gateway, and an operation with no implementation through a private driver.

lease.description: What the call does to a lease: takes it from the provider's answer, renews it, or releases it.

provider_scopes.description: The provider's own permissions, needed under delegated auth.

target.description: The resource a term's `targets` are checked against. Every operation names one, but one the runtime's own `store` implements: its target is the stream the runtime renders under the calling package (§4.8).

ConnectorOperation.title: ConnectorOperation

ConnectorPlacements.description: The placements a connector supports. A connector instance pins exactly one.
ConnectorPlacements.title: ConnectorPlacements

ContentDigest.description: A content digest with how it was taken and what it was taken over.
ContentDigest.title: ContentDigest

ContextLabels.description: How context may be read and where it may be shared. These labels never grant execution authority or manufacture a human decision.
ContextLabels.title: ContextLabels

ContextOrigin.description: Where a context entry came from: the artifact that holds it, the run and step that produced it, and its bytes' digest and size.

run_id.description: The run that produced it. An entry made outside any run, such as a host's supplied memory, or read from a store event, has none, and its `artifact_id` names it.

ContextOrigin.title: ContextOrigin

ContextProducer.description: The skill and method that produced a context entry.
ContextProducer.title: ContextProducer

audience.description: Hosts the runtime may present the credential to. A local store-only credential has none. For process-only use this is optional: delivery is to the bound executor, which owns further presentation. This field does not claim to confine a trusted process's network access.

delivery.description: How the local placement delivers the secret to an implementation. A lease has none: it never leaves runx Connect.

fields.description: The connect form, or for a lease the fields its take fills.

kind.description: The credential kind the hosted store checks (`api_key`, `oauth1_user`, `lease`, ...).

prefixes.description: Prefixes every value of this secret starts with, such as a provider's key prefix. Text that contains one carries the secret, and runx refuses to write it into a skill package.

Criterion.description: A check the runtime runs and binds to a receipt. The runtime is the only writer of criteria, so they are its own closed vocabulary: each names what was checked, and its binding states the result and the evidence.
Criterion.title: Criterion

CriterionBinding.description: One check's result and the references that prove it.
CriterionBinding.title: CriterionBinding

DecisionChoice.description: The decisions a governed call can carry out.
DecisionChoice.title: DecisionChoice

anyOf.description: Keep only this bounded evidence before acknowledgement custody. Each result member reads one path from the decoded provider response.

DelegatedAuth.description: A grant runx Connect brokers. Its principal request names whose authorization it holds, so one provider account holds one binding.
DelegatedAuth.title: DelegatedAuth

DigestAlgorithm.description: The algorithm a content digest was taken with.
DigestAlgorithm.title: DigestAlgorithm

DigestCommitment.description: An artifact's digest and how its bytes were canonicalized for it.
DigestCommitment.title: DigestCommitment

profile_digest.description: The digest of the profile that declares the offer at that version.

version.description: The package version the offer is sold at.

EnvironmentRequirementStatus.description: Safe environment readiness visible to an operating agent. The value is deliberately absent: models receive the requirement and its availability, never ambient or credential material.
EnvironmentRequirementStatus.title: EnvironmentRequirementStatus

EnvironmentRequirements.description: Environment names consumed by an executable act. Values are resolved only at execution time and never enter this declaration.
EnvironmentRequirements.title: EnvironmentRequirements

Evaluator.description: Who judged: the package and method of the step that returned the verdict, and the run it returned it in.
Evaluator.title: Evaluator

ExecutionLocation.description: Where the skill executes from on disk.
ExecutionLocation.title: ExecutionLocation

ExternalReferenceKind.description: The kinds of thing outside runx a connector's locators name: what its declared references classify and what its operations produce.
ExternalReferenceKind.title: ExternalReferenceKind

FileAppliedDelete.description: One file `fs.apply_bundle` deleted, or found already absent.

before_digest.description: What the file held before, when it existed.

diff.description: The unified diff from what the file held to its removal; empty when it was already absent.

FileAppliedDelete.title: FileAppliedDelete

before_digest.description: What the file held before, when it existed.

content_digest.description: The digest of what the file now holds.

diff.description: The unified diff from what the file held to what it holds now.

FileBundleDelete.description: A file a bundle deletes: its path, or its path with the digest of the content it removes.
FileBundleDelete.title: FileBundleDelete

create.description: The file must not exist yet.

expected_digest.description: The digest of the content it replaces, as a read returned it.

content_digest.description: The whole file's digest, which a write of it names.

credential.description: The stored credential used under credential custody.

anyOf.description: `Authorization: Bearer <credential field>`.
A declared credential field as the complete value of a fixed header. Unlike a request template, this is rendered only at secret delivery.

Exchange app credentials at a declared OAuth 2 token endpoint using client_secret_basic, then present its short-lived bearer token. Neither the credentials nor the token enter request templates/results.
OAuth 1.0a user context, signed with the credential's `consumer_key`, `consumer_secret`, `access_token` and `access_secret`.

A declared credential field as the request's complete URL, for a provider whose secret is the endpoint itself, such as a webhook. The request's declared URL is the prefix the credential's URL must start with.

A declared credential field placed in the request's JSON body at `pointer` (RFC 6901), for a provider that reads its key from the body, such as IndexNow. The body's literal object holds the pointer's parent and never sets it, and no input names it.

HttpAuth.description: How one credential authenticates a request.
HttpAuth.title: HttpAuth

HttpImplementation.description: An HTTP exchange the native runtime performs. Bodies are JSON; the transport carries text, so no byte or multipart body is expressible.

auth.description: How each credential the operation accepts authenticates a request, by credential name; the instance's credential picks its entry. With none, requests carry no credential.

decode.description: How an answer is decoded; JSON unless declared.

rate_limit.description: How the provider says when a rate limit lifts.

result_paths.description: Where each result field comes from. An operation with one result field takes the whole decoded answer unless this says otherwise; validation writes that default in.

HttpImplementation.title: HttpImplementation

HttpPageCursor.description: Where a page names the next page's cursor, and how the next request carries it.

cursor.description: Where a decoded page names the next cursor.

in.description: Cursor placement. Body placement retains the cursor's JSON type.

param.description: Query parameter name, or an object-member JSON pointer when `in` is body.

HttpPageCursor.title: HttpPageCursor

HttpPages.description: A read answered in pages. The request is sent again with the cursor each page names until a page names none, a page holds no items, or the items gathered reach `limit`. The pages decode to `{items, next}`: every page's items in order, and the cursor a further read would start from, or null once the read reached the end. Repeated requests additionally return `started` and `complete` for each item: an exhausted shared budget can leave later items unstarted, which must never be interpreted as no matches. Each item settles on its own, with `error` null unless it failed: one that fails reports its `error`, keeping what it read and the cursor it stopped at, and the rest go on, unless the provider refused the caller, as a rate limit does, which leaves the rest unstarted.

items.description: Where a decoded page holds its items.

limit.description: How many items the caller asked for. Absent, or rendered from an argument the call does not carry, every page is read.

next.description: Where the next page comes from.

HttpPages.title: HttpPages

body.description: The body template; JSON unless `body_encoding` declares a form.

body_encoding.description: The wire representation of a request's body. Forms render a flat object of string, number and boolean values; nested form names are literal keys.

each.description: Send this request once per element of the array this renders to, binding the element as `{"$item": ...}`. A read decodes the answers as an array in the same order; a write is a repeated write, one outcome per element. Bounded by the input schema's `maxItems`.

id.description: Names the request, unique within the exchange, so a later request reads its answer as `{"$response": "<id>.<path>"}`. A lone request needs no name. Readbacks address what a write returned as `{"$response": "write.<path>"}`; `write` is reserved for that.

pages.description: A read whose answer comes in pages.

Implementation.description: What one operation does, written as a single-key map: `{http: ...}`, `{mcp: ...}`, `{process: ...}`, `{web: {}}`, `{store: {}}` or `{artifact: {}}`. The local placement runs every kind; the hosted placement runs `http`.
Implementation.title: Implementation

InspectedOperation.description: One operation of a connector, as a caller decides on it.

access.description: `read` or `mutate`, when the project holds the connector.

approval_required.description: Whether every call waits on the person's approval of its exact input, when the project holds the connector.

InspectedOperation.title: InspectedOperation

anyOf.description: A runx Connect grant. Hosted placement only.

The named connector credential, held by the secret the operator keeps in runx under `secret` (`runx secret set`): stored in the runx home, or read through a secrets manager by reference. Every call reads it again, so setting it anew serves without binding again. `proof` is an HMAC keyed by the binding operator's runx home over the whole binding, the proof left out: a project store can neither name the operator's secret nor widen a binding. `scopes` is what the operator grants it.

The named connector credential, read on every call from the variable its declaration delivers it in, in the process environment or the workspace `.env`. The instance holds the variable's name, never its value, so a key rotated there serves without binding again. `scopes` is what the operator grants it, as for a stored credential.

A local session the runtime can identify. A command session pins its account in the instance's `account_id`. `scopes` is what the operator grants it: every scope its credential serves unless narrowed when it was confirmed. The provider enforces the account's own permissions.

What a purchase bought (S10, N11): one resource's credential, held by runx Connect for the principal and presented only to the requests of operations on that resource. Admission pins it for one call, by the target the call names; it is never confirmed or selected. Hosted placement only.
A public API; reads only.

InstanceAuthority.description: Where the principal's authority over the provider is held.
InstanceAuthority.title: InstanceAuthority

Intent.description: Why an act was done and under what it was legitimate.

legitimacy.description: The execution term the act was admitted under.

Intent.title: Intent

LeaseRelease.description: A release: the leased credential, whose resource is gone.
LeaseRelease.title: LeaseRelease

LeaseRenew.description: A renew: the leased credential and its new expiry, one `$result` binding.
LeaseRenew.title: LeaseRenew

LeaseTake.description: A take: the `kind: lease` credential, the new resource's target rendered from the call's public result, when it ends, and each of the credential's fields filled from the provider's raw answer.

expires_at.description: When the resource ends, one `$result` binding.

fields.description: Each field of the credential and the one `$response` binding that fills it.

LeaseTake.title: LeaseTake

Lineage.description: What runx committed of a receipt's place among others.

children.description: The receipts of the subject's direct children, each committed by its id and signed-body digest.

Lineage.title: Lineage

LoadedMethod.description: One method of a loaded skill, as a model chooses it.

bound.description: Whether this load bound it, so the turn offers it as a tool.

purpose.description: What it does and when to use it, as its package states it.

LoadedMethod.title: LoadedMethod

LoadedMethodInput.description: One input of a loaded skill's method.
LoadedMethodInput.title: LoadedMethodInput

skill.description: The ref each of its tools names: the canonical `<publisher>/<name>@<version>` of a registry skill, or the project's path.

manifest_digest.description: The manifest each of its operations runs; one that changed since the load is refused.

LoadedPackage.description: The package a load bound. A project's own package has no tier and no publisher.
LoadedPackage.title: LoadedPackage

mcp_server.description: Required when any operation uses an `mcp` implementation.

McpImplementation.description: A tool on the connector's MCP server. The tool is pinned by its served definition; the manifest's verb, not the tool's annotations, is enforced.

arguments.description: Rendered from the call input into the tool arguments. A multiplexed tool's discriminating argument is a literal here, never an input.

readback.description: How a write is confirmed: an independent call to a read tool, checked against what the write returned. Every write has one; a read has none.

tool_digest.description: sha256 over the served tool's name, description, input schema and annotations when the manifest was authored. A tool served with another definition is refused.

McpImplementation.title: McpImplementation

McpReadback.description: The read tool call that confirms an MCP write. Its arguments may bind the write's result as `{"$response": "write.<path>"}`.
McpReadback.title: McpReadback

auth.description: How each credential authenticates the session, by credential name: a bearer token. With none, the session carries no credential.

headers.description: Headers every request of a session carries, rendered from the call (a tenant or brand the server selects by header). A header whose argument the call does not carry is not sent. Calls that render different headers run on different sessions.

anyOf.description: A server the runtime starts as a declared trusted host process and speaks to over stdio. `command` is found on the child's `PATH`. The instance's credential reaches it in the variable its declaration names, as a process implementation's does.

McpServer.description: The MCP server a connector's local `mcp` implementations call.
McpServer.title: McpServer

MethodInspection.description: One method as a caller reads it: what it takes, what it returns, and what it needs.

connectors.description: The connector requirements of the skill, by key.

environment.description: The environment variables the method reads, by name.

input_schema.description: Its inputs as one JSON schema, with the method's examples.

packets.description: The packet each result output declares, by output name, the whole result's under the name of the output it is.

schemas.description: Its derived input and output schemas and their digests.

MethodInspection.title: MethodInspection

MethodSchemas.description: A method's input and output JSON Schemas, derived from its fields, and the canonical digest of each: what a paid method's listing, purchases and receipts bind.
MethodSchemas.title: MethodSchemas

MissingFile.description: A file `fs.read_bundle` could not read, and why.
MissingFile.title: MissingFile

OperationAmount.description: An exact amount an operation moves, in the provider's smallest unit.
OperationAmount.title: OperationAmount

OperationCost.description: A provider's charge for one call. A missing USD quote is metered usage whose monetary price is unknown; `usd_micro: 0` explicitly declares free. No declaration at all means no charge is known, which is not a quote of zero: a money limit admits only a known quote. The quote and basis are authority-bound.

source_url.description: The page that states it, `https` only.

OperationCost.title: OperationCost

OperationEffect.description: What a write produced: one reference, or one per element of a result array. The locator is rendered from the call's arguments, the instance's parameters and the call's result (`$result`); under `each` it reads the element as `$item`. A repeated write's result array is its items' outcomes: an effect is rendered for each applied item, whose `$item` is the provider's answer, and an item not applied produced nothing. Where the connector declares `references`, the kind is one of them and every locator matches its pattern.

each.description: A `$result` pointer to the array the effect repeats over.

OperationEffect.title: OperationEffect

OperationIntent.description: An operation call before admission: everything a grant, a delegation or a person is asked to cover. Its digest is the one identity of the call: the execution term, the approval, the idempotency key and the receipt all bind it, so a call that changes in any of these fields is a new call.

act_digest.description: Digest of the act the call performs, when its caller states one.

amount.description: Present when the operation requires an amount.

approval_digest.description: Digest of the approval text a person is shown, when the call is gated.

instance_id.description: The instance fixes the placement, principal and account.

operation_digest.description: What the operation means: its verb, scopes, target and floors.

request_key_digest.description: Digest of the caller's request key; present for mutations.

OperationIntent.title: OperationIntent

anyOf.description: This call creates the resource and takes its credential.
This call moves the lease's expiry.
This call ends the lease: the resource is gone.

OperationLease.description: What a hosted call does to a lease (S10, N11): a credential the provider issues for one resource a call creates, held by runx Connect for the resource's owner. Connect applies it at the provider's answer, so a leased value never reaches the kernel, which sees only the lease's evidence (its target, expiry and the value's digest). A lease is keyed by connector, credential and target, so a seller leases resources only in its own connector. Each action carries only what it needs: a take names the new resource, and a renew or a release acts on the operation's own target.
OperationLease.title: OperationLease

OperationTarget.description: The target an operation acts on, rendered from the call's arguments and the instance's parameters. The rendered value must equal the admitted target.

pattern.description: A regular expression the rendered target must match whole, for a connector whose targets have a shape authority compares, such as a conversation locator.

OperationTarget.title: OperationTarget

OperationVerb.description: The authority verbs an operation may declare. `read` makes the operation a read; every other verb makes it a mutation. `delete` stays its own verb because a grant that serves a delete or a revoke is a destructive one, and a targeted grant matches only a request of its own kind. What kind of write it is, a comment or a merge, is its `scopes`' to say.
OperationVerb.title: OperationVerb

OperationalProposalRedactionStatus.description: How far a source packet's content was redacted before it crossed into the packet.
OperationalProposalRedactionStatus.title: OperationalProposalRedactionStatus

OutputField.description: One output field: its JSON Schema, `optional: true` when a producer may leave it out, and the `packet` it is kept as.
OutputField.title: OutputField

PaidSkillExecutorBinding.description: An exact execution package: the skill and method, and the digests of the package and closure that run.

package_digest.description: The execution package digest a run records (`runx.skill-package.v1` over the files a run loads), not the registry's digest of the published package files that a listing binds.

PaidSkillExecutorBinding.title: PaidSkillExecutorBinding

anyOf.description: One amount for every call.

An amount for each combination of values of the priced inputs, each an `enum` input the method requires. Each case names every priced input by name, and the cases cover every combination exactly once.
A base amount plus a unit amount for each started `unit_bytes` of the committed artifact the `input` holds, up to `max_bytes`.

PaidSkillPrice.description: How an offer prices one call: from the listing and the inputs the method receives, never from the method. Cloud and the buyer's kernel compute the same amount, so nothing the buyer or the seller's method says can change it.
PaidSkillPrice.title: PaidSkillPrice

PaidSkillPriceCase.description: One `by_input` case: the value each priced input takes, by name, and what a call with them costs.
PaidSkillPriceCase.title: PaidSkillPriceCase

PaymentCompatibility.description: Constraints on a candidate payment method. These declarations filter discovery; the selected operation still admits the exact payment and account.

currencies.description: Quoted currencies; an omitted restriction leaves validation to the provider's exact operation, rather than inventing an FX conversion.

networks.description: Protocol network identifiers, such as the CAIP-2 `eip155:8453`.

payment_methods.description: Protocol payment method identifiers, such as `stripe` or `tempo` for MPP.

PaymentCompatibility.title: PaymentCompatibility

Pinned.description: Something named exactly: its `ref` and its exact `revision`.
Pinned.title: Pinned

PolicyLintEngine.description: The engine that linted the policy.
PolicyLintEngine.title: PolicyLintEngine

PolicyLintStatus.description: Whether the policy parsed and linted clean.
PolicyLintStatus.title: PolicyLintStatus

PrincipalRequest.description: The request that names whose authority a session or a delegated grant holds, sent with that authority as a bearer credential.

id.description: Where the answer carries the account's stable id.

login.description: Where the answer carries the account's name.

url.description: An `https` URL the authority may be sent to: for a session, a host in its credential's audience; for a delegated grant, a host its hosted operations reach.

PrincipalRequest.title: PrincipalRequest

message.description: Why it failed, for a process that never ran or whose supervisor ended without recording its exit.

ProcessImplementation.description: A tool package that runs as this operation's implementation, receiving the operation's credential. It is a declared trusted host process.

readback.description: How a write is confirmed: the tool is run again with `phase: readback` and the acknowledgement, and what it observes must match.

requires.description: What the runtime grants the tool, such as `fs:write`.

result_from.description: The bounded public answer to return after confirmation. A durable acknowledgement can remain just an opaque provider reference.

ProcessImplementation.title: ProcessImplementation

ProcessKind.description: What a process is: one `process.start` detached under a supervisor of its own, or a `command.execute` its driver runs and follows until its call settles. A command takes no input.
ProcessKind.title: ProcessKind

ProcessReadback.description: What a process tool's readback must match.
ProcessReadback.title: ProcessReadback

ProcessState.description: Where a process stands: recorded and waiting on its supervisor, running under it, or exited.
ProcessState.title: ProcessState

ProcessStream.description: A process's stdout or stderr, or the terminal a `tty` process writes to.
ProcessStream.title: ProcessStream

ProfileFile.description: A resolved profile sourced from a workspace file (memory, conventions, voice).
ProfileFile.title: ProfileFile

ProjectBinding.description: A skill package of the person's own, as a run binds it (D30): it is `project:<name>`, and one directory is that package in the run.

directory.description: Its directory: relative to the workspace when within it, else absolute.

ProjectBinding.title: ProjectBinding

PurchaseCanonicalizerVersion.description: The sole V1 canonicalization identifier for digest-bound inputs.
PurchaseCanonicalizerVersion.title: PurchaseCanonicalizerVersion

PurchaseFailure.description: Bounded, customer-safe reason a refund won the outcome gate.
PurchaseFailure.title: PurchaseFailure

PurchaseLease.description: One resource a fulfilled purchase bought, held by runx for the purchase's buyer (S10, N11): where it is held and until when, and the digest of the held value, which tells holds apart without showing one.
PurchaseLease.title: PurchaseLease

anyOf.description: The account's runx balance, which covers the price: the price moves inside runx's ledger, with no settlement per call.
A hosted payment grant whose connector pays on the quote's network and asset.

PurchaseMethod.description: One way the buyer can pay. An answer's `choice` names it: the balance by `runx:balance`, a payment grant by the choice binding its instance and quoted option.
PurchaseMethod.title: PurchaseMethod

protocol_version.description: Present only when the payment protocol carries a version.

PurchasePaymentMethod.description: Protocol-owned discovery and display terms. These do not authorize a payment: the settlement executor verifies the complete challenge itself.
PurchasePaymentMethod.title: PurchasePaymentMethod

PurchasePaymentOptionBinding.description: One exact quoted option. Its provider attempt retains this binding through settlement and recovery; this is not another payment or purchase identity.
PurchasePaymentOptionBinding.title: PurchasePaymentOptionBinding

PurchaseQuote.description: The quote decided on, including its protocol-owned display terms and the exact challenge binding. An absent network is not an EVM network default.
PurchaseQuote.title: PurchaseQuote

PurchaseRequest.description: What a person decides when a call reaches a paid method: one quote's exact offer version, seller and price, and each payment method that can pay it. The request's digest binds all of it, so an answer pays only this quote, before it expires.

methods.description: Never empty: a call no method can pay fails instead of asking.

package_digest.description: The execution package digest the purchase runs (`runx.skill-package.v1` over the files a run loads), not the registry's digest of the published package files that a listing binds.

PurchaseRequest.title: PurchaseRequest

RateLimit.description: How a provider says when a rate limit lifts. A rate limited request (an HTTP 429) stops a repeated write, and the outcome carries the time.

reset_header.description: The response header holding the Unix second the limit lifts at.

RateLimit.title: RateLimit

anyOf.description: A field of the write's acknowledgement, which must be present.
A field of the call's own arguments, so the write is checked against what was approved. A match whose argument the call does not carry is not checked: nothing was asked for that field.
A field of the item a repeated write was sent for, checked the same way as an argument.

An exact expected value rendered from approved arguments and the projected acknowledgement (`$response: write.json.<path>`). Useful for provider resource locators and structured relationship evidence.

ReadbackExpected.description: What a confirming read's field must equal.
ReadbackExpected.title: ReadbackExpected

ReceiptAct.description: What was done, inline. The act's semantic core (intent, the caller's reason, the checks bound to it) stays in the signed body; its outcome is the receipt's seal. Only the bulky execution I/O (the agent-context envelope: instructions/inputs/output and tool calls) is referenced via `context_ref` and hydrated by projections.

context_ref.description: The agent-context envelope (instructions/inputs/output/tool-calls) is referenced here and hydrated by the inspection projections.

operation.description: The connector operation the act ran, exactly as admission bound it: its qualified connector, manifest and connector digests, and the operation, instance and target it was admitted for.

previous.description: The receipt the caller states this act follows. It is the caller's statement, recorded as given: runx does not check it.

reason.description: What the caller told a reader about this particular call, when it said anything.

ReceiptAct.title: ReceiptAct

actor_ref.description: The principal an act was admitted for, when the run was given one. A receipt with no admitted actor states none.

derivations.description: How each derived execution term in `terms` was proven.

grant_refs.description: The capability evidence that admitted the receipt's effects: a runx Connect grant, or the local connector instance the operator confirmed.

ReceiptCanonicalization.description: The canonicalization byte contract a receipt's id and digest commit under. v1 has one.
ReceiptCanonicalization.title: ReceiptCanonicalization

ReceiptEnforcement.description: What the runtime enforced around the subject.

execution_boundary.description: Where the subject ran, when the runtime observed it.

ReceiptEnforcement.title: ReceiptEnforcement

runx_version.description: The runx release that issued the receipt.

ReceiptProofDecision.description: Whether every requested receipt resolved and verified.
ReceiptProofDecision.title: ReceiptProofDecision

ReceiptProofStore.description: The receipt store a proof read.
ReceiptProofStore.title: ReceiptProofStore

ReceiptProofVerification.description: A proof's tree verification, which it always runs.
ReceiptProofVerification.title: ReceiptProofVerification

ReceiptQuerySource.description: Where a query read its receipts.
ReceiptQuerySource.title: ReceiptQuerySource

ReceiptQueryVerification.description: A query's tree verification; `intact` is null when it was not asked for.
ReceiptQueryVerification.title: ReceiptQueryVerification

ReceiptReadStatus.description: Availability of the retained claim. Every returned receipt has verified first; these states do not claim that an unavailable payload was read.
ReceiptReadStatus.title: ReceiptReadStatus

ReferenceDeclaration.description: One kind of thing a connector's locators name.

locator.description: A regular expression the whole locator matches.

ReferenceDeclaration.title: ReferenceDeclaration

ReferenceType.description: What a reference points at. External kinds never name a provider: the reference's `provider` and `locator` say where, and connectors declare which of their locators are which kind.
ReferenceType.title: ReferenceType

RequiredLease.description: The lease a buyer must hold to buy a paid method, such as the inbox an extension extends: only a buyer holding that lease, on the resource the method's inputs name, may buy, so the buyer hands the seller's run no bearer. It is checked before the quote and again before payment.

connector.description: The seller connector that holds the lease.

target.description: The leased resource, rendered from the method's inputs alone.

RequiredLease.title: RequiredLease

outputs.description: The call's output as project artifacts of its run: one per packet output, and one for the rest.

reason.description: Why a call that ran did not succeed.

anyOf.description: Admission refused the call; nothing ran.
The call could not run.
Claimed and not settled: its effect may have happened.

RunCallOutcome.description: How a call stood when this event recorded it.
RunCallOutcome.title: RunCallOutcome

RunCallOutput.description: A project artifact holding part of a call's output.

output.description: The packet output it holds; absent on the artifact of the call's other outputs.

RunCallOutput.title: RunCallOutput

RunClose.description: Seal the run without continuing it: a person stopped it, or a new attempt replaced it. An effect the run left unconfirmed stays unconfirmed.
RunClose.title: RunClose

RunDriver.description: Who works a run's agent turns, fixed when it starts: the host it is attached to, or runx's managed agent.
RunDriver.title: RunDriver

call_id.description: The id its host pinned on the call.

standing.description: The standing approval that admitted it on the approval floor, when one did.

turn.description: The address of the turn the call was made in.

anyOf.description: The person replaced the run's standing approvals for every later step.
A resume admitted a person's decision on the request at `address`, before it took the run further; the run's next driver to reach the request uses it.
On a request it raised.
On a bounded retry; the step has not started.
On its retry after it was claimed: it reaches the world, and its effect may have happened.
On what the child run it started waits on.

RunListEntry.description: One run of a listing, read from its first and latest events.

pending_request_id.description: The request a paused run's step is held on: its turn's act, or what it asked.

RunListEntry.title: RunListEntry

RunOutcome.description: How a run, or a receipt's subject, ended.
RunOutcome.title: RunOutcome

driven.description: Whether a process holds the run's driver lock now. A host that restarts reconciles once this is false.

package_digest.description: The execution package digest of the package the run loaded, not the registry's digest of the published package files a listing carries.

RunState.description: Where a run stands, from its latest event alone.
RunState.title: RunState

description.description: A skill's description, from the frontmatter of its own `SKILL.md`.

methods.description: A skill's methods, each with its purpose when its `run.yaml` states one.

packets.description: The outputs it keeps as artifacts, each with its packet.

visibility.description: A skill's catalog visibility; public when its manifest declares none.

RunxListOutputPacket.description: An output kept as an artifact, and its packet.
RunxListOutputPacket.title: RunxListOutputPacket

RunxListVisibility.description: Whether a host may offer a skill to a person or an agent. An internal skill, such as a workflow stage, runs only as part of the skill that owns it.
RunxListVisibility.title: RunxListVisibility

Seal.description: Exactly one seal. `deferred` expresses a suspended (waiting/delegated) run. It closes when the receipt is created, so the receipt's `created_at` is its one time.

reason.description: Why it ended so, where the outcome alone does not say.

Seal.title: Seal

SealReason.description: Why a receipt's subject ended as it did, beyond its outcome.
SealReason.title: SealReason

anyOf.description: A token printed by a command-line tool the person is signed into, such as `gh auth token`. The runtime runs the command when an instance is confirmed and before each call, never stores the token, and delivers it as the named credential.

command.description: The program, found on `PATH` and run without a shell, and its arguments.

credential.description: The one-field credential the token stands in for.

principal.description: The request that names whose token it is.

anyOf.description: A CLI that keeps its own credential and refresh lifecycle. The command returns only public account JSON; process implementations use that same CLI and must enforce the pinned principal at credential use.
A signed-in browser profile. Its installed tool receives `operation: session` and the instance parameters and returns the rendered account as `{id, login}`. No session secret is exported.

SessionAuth.description: A local session: authority the person already holds on this machine.
SessionAuth.title: SessionAuth

SignalAuthenticity.description: Who vouches for a source's arrival, and on what evidence.
SignalAuthenticity.title: SignalAuthenticity

SignalTrustLevel.description: How far a source's arrival is vouched for.
SignalTrustLevel.title: SignalTrustLevel

SkillAllowance.description: One entry of an allowance's `skills`: a child skill by name, or a catalog rule, which admits the skills and connectors a `load` call finds.
SkillAllowance.title: SkillAllowance

SkillCatalog.description: How a catalog files the package.
SkillCatalog.title: SkillCatalog

SkillCatalogEntry.description: One skill or tool an authored skill can reuse.
SkillCatalogEntry.title: SkillCatalogEntry

SkillManual.description: A skill's manual: its `SKILL.md` exactly as its package holds it, the skill's operating guidance. A host gives it to its model as guidance, below the host's own instructions and runx's governance, which it never widens, and never as a tool result's data.
SkillManual.title: SkillManual

SkillPackageFile.description: One file of a skill package.
SkillPackageFile.title: SkillPackageFile

SkillValidationVerdict.description: How far validating a package got.
SkillValidationVerdict.title: SkillValidationVerdict

StandingApproval.description: A person's bounded confirmation of the writes a run under `effects: ask` would otherwise hold for them: exactly one of `edits`, `commands`, `operations` and `local`. It never covers a write's own approval, an operation's declared one or a step's.

commands.description: A command or process whose argv begins with these tokens.

operations.description: A connector operation's write that these names cover.

StandingApproval.title: StandingApproval

argv_prefix.description: The exact leading argv tokens. Argv has no shell, so a prefix admits nothing beyond the tokens it names.

paths.description: Workspace-relative path prefixes, by whole components; `""` is the whole workspace.

names.description: Connector operations as `<connector>/<operation>`, or every operation of exactly one connector as `<connector>/*`.

StoreAppended.description: An append that committed or replayed.
StoreAppended.title: StoreAppended

StoreAppliedStatus.description: An append that landed: `committed`, or `replayed`, the same idempotency key with the same event, answered as the first time.
StoreAppliedStatus.title: StoreAppliedStatus

StoreBackend.description: The backend that served an answer.
StoreBackend.title: StoreBackend

StoreConflictStatus.description: An append that appended nothing: `version_conflict`, the key wasn't at the expected version, retried after a read; or `idempotency_conflict`, the idempotency key was used for a different event, checked first and never retried.
StoreConflictStatus.title: StoreConflictStatus

StoreConflicted.description: An append that conflicted, appending nothing.
StoreConflicted.title: StoreConflicted

committed_at.description: When the store committed it; a fact's own date is in its data.

digest.description: Covers the writer, the type and the data.

id.description: A length-delimited encoding of stream, key and version.

type.description: Declared by the writer, never guessed.

writer.description: The package that wrote it and the digest of the exact bytes it ran from, set by the runtime: every event records one.

StoreEventRef.description: The event an append committed or replayed.
StoreEventRef.title: StoreEventRef

StoreImplementation.description: The runtime's event store: append-only streams with an expected version and an idempotency key per append, a rolling projection per stream, and stream heads by latest event. The instance's `url` parameter chooses SQLite, Postgres or Redis; without one it is the workspace store.
StoreImplementation.title: StoreImplementation

StoreInspected.description: A key's version, its newest event whole, and its chain.

last_event.description: The key's newest event, or null at version 0.

StoreInspected.title: StoreInspected

StoreListed.description: One page of a stream's keys, newest commit first.

keys.description: At most 100, a listing's largest page.

next_cursor.description: Where the next page starts, or null when there's no further page.

StoreListed.title: StoreListed

StoreListedKey.description: A listed key and its newest event.
StoreListedKey.title: StoreListedKey

StoreMatch.description: A key a search matched, by its newest event.
StoreMatch.title: StoreMatch

StoreRead.description: One page of a key's events, in version order.

events.description: At most 500, a read's largest page.

last_version.description: The last version in this page, which the next read passes as `after_version`; with no events, the version read after.

StoreRead.title: StoreRead

StoreSearched.description: One page of a search of one stream's current entries, in score order with ties by key.

matches.description: At most 100, a search's largest page.

StoreSearched.title: StoreSearched

StoreWriter.description: Who wrote an event: the package and the digest of the exact bytes it ran from, set by the runtime, never by a caller.
StoreWriter.title: StoreWriter

outcome_digest.description: The digest of how the subject ended: its seal's outcome, the outputs it declared, and its direct children's receipt ids. The receipt commits to that; the produced content beyond its declared outputs is not part of it.

SubjectKind.description: What a receipt seals: one step's attempt, or the whole workflow a run ran.
SubjectKind.title: SubjectKind

TerminalSize.description: A terminal's size, in character cells.
TerminalSize.title: TerminalSize

ToolProcess.description: A tool's executable: a trusted host process, the same object as a step's process tool. runx controls its argv, cwd, environment and lifetime, but does not confine it.

environment.description: Environment names consumed by an executable act. Values are resolved only at execution time and never enter this declaration.

ToolProcess.title: ToolProcess

TrustTier.description: How far the registry vouches for a publisher: runx's own packages, a publisher it verified, or anyone's.
TrustTier.title: TrustTier

TurnAllowance.description: The calls an open turn admits: the skill's declared limits.

asks.description: Whether the turn may ask the human.

skills.description: Child skills by ref, and the catalog rules a load is admitted under.

TurnAllowance.title: TurnAllowance

anyOf.description: The call ran and succeeded.

artifacts.description: Each packet output as a project artifact of the run, by output name: a reference a later call passes in place of the packet.

anyOf.description: The call ran and failed, with its receipt; or it failed before it could run.
Admission refused the call; nothing ran.

The call has not settled. `waiting` is what it waits on, each request by its address: its own ask or approval, its retry while its effect is unconfirmed, or what the child run it started waits on, including that run's open turns. The call settles when those are answered.

TurnContextLine.description: One context entry of an act as a model reads it in an index: what it is, whom it may be shared with, how large it is, and the locator `turn_read` reads its data by.
TurnContextLine.title: TurnContextLine

TurnRequirement.description: What a turn can need from the agent harness that works it.
TurnRequirement.title: TurnRequirement

anyOf.description: A child skill: one the allowance names, run by its default method, or one method of a skill a load bound, run as the load bound it.
The call's input is `{reason}`; the human approves or declines it.
The call's input is `{skill, method?}` or `{connector}`: a package a catalog rule admits, whose methods or operations the turn offers from then on.

TurnTarget.description: What a turn call names: one entry of the turn's allowance.
TurnTarget.title: TurnTarget

TurnTool.description: One call an open turn offers its agent: an allowance entry, named for MCP, with the input it takes.

name.description: Distinct within the turn, in the MCP tool-name grammar.

TurnTool.title: TurnTool

TurnView.description: An agent act as its turn's agent reads it. What the act allows it shows once, as the status's tools, by the names a call takes: the act's declared allowance names a catalog tool as the catalog does (`fs.read`), which is not the name a call takes (`fs_read`).

context_kinds.description: The kinds of context the turn asks its host to supply.

requires.description: What the turn needs from its agent harness.

TurnView.title: TurnView

TurnViewEnvelope.description: An act's envelope as its turn's agent reads it: whole, except that each context entry is a line of an index, its data read by `turn_read`. The act's instructions and inputs stay whole, as the act itself; each input also reads by its ref.
TurnViewEnvelope.title: TurnViewEnvelope

UnreadableRun.description: A run the listing found and couldn't read, such as one another runx version recorded: listed by its id, so one record never hides the rest.

reason.description: Why its record can't be read.

UnreadableRun.title: UnreadableRun

VerdictAnswer.description: An answer: to one criterion, or for the whole.
VerdictAnswer.title: VerdictAnswer

VerdictCriterion.description: One check: its stable id, whether it's required, and the question that must be answered yes.
VerdictCriterion.title: VerdictCriterion

WaitedRequest.description: A request the run waits on: its address, the digest an answer binds to, and the request itself.
WaitedRequest.title: WaitedRequest

WebImplementation.description: The runtime's guarded public web read: one URL fetched with GET, redirects admitted against the call's host allowlist, private networks refused, the body bounded and extracted as text, metadata or links.
WebImplementation.title: WebImplementation

due_after_seconds.description: Relative scheduling for a successor emitted after an external effect. The operator resolves it against the time it admits that successor.

WorkState.description: Where the work stands after the run: done, waiting on a follow-up, or held.
WorkState.title: WorkState

description: Every runx contract type that has no document of its own, each defined once. The documents beside this one refer to these definitions.
